projectTitle: gplay — Google Play Developer Publishing CLI
description: A non-interactive CLI for the Google Play Developer Publishing API (Android Publisher v3): upload AABs and APKs, move builds between tracks, run and halt staged rollouts, edit store listings and images, manage in-app products and subscriptions, and read reviews and orders. Authenticates with a Google service account key and follows Play's transactional edit model. Built for scripts and AI agents, with the complete reference embedded in the binary behind `gplay llm`.
rules: Authentication uses a Google service account key registered with `gplay configure` and selected by --profile or GPLAY_PROFILE. The service account must be granted API access in Play Console under Users and permissions; a 401 or 403 means that grant is missing rather than the key being malformed.

An app must have had at least one APK or AAB uploaded through the Play Console UI before the API can touch it. Until then every call 404s on the package — that is expected, not a bug, and cannot be worked around through the API.
Version codes must increase. Re-uploading an existing version code fails, and Play orders releases by version code, not by version name.

Changes are transactional: open an edit, apply changes against it, then commit. An edit that is never committed changes nothing, and a stale edit is rejected — a change that appears not to have applied is usually an uncommitted edit.

Promoting a release to production, changing a staged rollout percentage, or halting a release changes what real users receive immediately. Use --dry-run first, and treat the rollout fraction as a decision rather than a parameter.
The package name comes from -p / --package or GPLAY_PACKAGE. Most commands need it, and pointing at the wrong package is indistinguishable from a permissions problem in the error output.
--json prints the raw API JSON; the default output is a human-readable table. Parse only the JSON.
The complete reference is embedded in the binary: `gplay llm` (Markdown) or `gplay llm --format json`. It is regenerated from the cobra command tree, so prefer it over any remembered command list.
